key_insight: Open-weight LLMs can reliably turn CAV vulnerability text into structured STIX and CWE outputs, but full ATT&CK-style attack mapping is still much harder.
engineering_relevance: This work helps security teams automate threat intelligence for autonomous vehicles, improving prioritization of vulnerable assets, weaknesses, and likely attack behaviors.
method: Built CAV-STIXGen, a dataset linking CAV CVE descriptions to STIX objects, CWE labels, and MITRE ATT&CK mappings.
Benchmarked 11 open-weight LLMs (4B–120B) across prompting strategies and temperatures.
Compared single-model and multi-agent configurations for structured threat extraction.
evidence_signal: Single-model setups reached F1 scores of 0.94 for STIX domain objects, 0.63 for relationship objects, and 0.99 for CWE mapping, while multi-agent results reached 0.91 for SDOs and 0.43 for SROs.
watch_item: MITRE ATT&CK mapping remains incomplete and relationship extraction is weaker, so outputs should be validated before operational use.
paper_title: Evaluating Open-Weight LLMs for Generating Structured Threat Information for Autonomous Vehicle Vulnerabilities
